name: f2fs_resize_fs
prose: Precondition: filp is an open file on a mounted f2fs filesystem and block_count is the requested new size in blocks (gc.c:2314-2454; only shrinking is supported). Postcondition: returns an int, 0 on success or a negative errno; it has these return statements: -EINVAL at 2325 if block_count exceeds the current block_count; -EINVAL at 2333 on a multi-device fs when the new size would not reach into the last device; -EINVAL at 2339 if block_count is not a multiple of the section size; 0 at 2342 if block_count equals the current count (nothing done); -EFSCORRUPTED at 2346 if SBI_NEED_FSCK is set; -EINVAL at 2351 if DISABLE_CHECKPOINT is on; the mnt_want_write_file error at 2356; at 2388 the error left after the first phase (-EAGAIN if gc_lock cannot be taken with trylock, -ENOSPC if the shrunk size plus valid user blocks, reserved blocks, unusable blocks and root-reserved blocks exceed user_block_count, or the error of free_segment_range(sbi, secs, true)); the freeze_super error at 2392; the thaw_super error at 2397 or -EROFS at 2398 if the fs is read-only after freezing; and 'return err' at 2453. First phase: under gc_lock (write-trylock) and f2fs_lock_op, it checks the space condition and runs free_segment_range in dry-run mode, then unlocks and drops write access. Second phase: freeze_super, then under gc_lock and cp_global_sem it rechecks the space condition and, if it holds, reduces sbi->user_block_count by the shrunk blocks, sets SBI_IS_RESIZEFS, runs free_segment_range(sbi, secs, false) (error: recover_out), update_sb_metadata(-secs), f2fs_commit_super (error: restore the sb metadata and recover_out), update_fs_metadata(-secs), sets SBI_IS_DIRTY and calls f2fs_write_checkpoint with cp_control CP_RESIZE (error: undo the fs and sb metadata and commit the super again). recover_out clears SBI_IS_RESIZEFS and, if err, sets SBI_NEED_FSCK, logs 'resize_fs failed, should run fsck to repair!' and adds shrunk_blocks back to user_block_count. out_err (reached also from the second-phase -ENOSPC without touching user_block_count) releases cp_global_sem and gc_lock, calls thaw_super (its result ignored) and returns err.
note: slice cut head (function at 2314-2454, slice 2323-2454). Unreviewed originally; checked against the full function. Note the second-phase -ENOSPC (2408) goes to out_err and does not run recover_out, so no NEED_FSCK flag and no user_block_count restore in that case (nothing was subtracted).

name: f2fs_get_victim
prose: Precondition: sbi is a valid f2fs_sb_info; result points to an unsigned int holding NULL_SEGNO or a hint victim segment; gc_type is BG_GC or FG_GC, type, alloc_mode and age select the policy, one_time selects one-time GC (gc.c:766-969). The caller does not hold dirty_i->seglist_lock (it is taken here). Postcondition: returns 0 when a victim was selected and *result is set (or already was the hint), -ENODATA when none is available, -EBUSY when the hinted section is in use; the only return is 'return ret' at 968 after mutex_unlock. It takes seglist_lock, builds a victim_sel_policy (select_policy, min_cost = get_max_cost). With a hint (*result != NULL_SEGNO): -ENODATA if the segment has no valid blocks (get_valid_blocks == 0), -EBUSY if sec_usage_check says its section is in use, else for FG_GC it clears the section's bit in victim_secmap, takes the hint as min_segno and goes to got_result. Without a hint: -ENODATA if p.max_search == 0; for large sections with LFS it first consumes sbi->next_victim_seg[BG_GC] (or [FG_GC] for foreground GC), clearing that field and setting *result; for LFS and FG_GC it tries check_bg_victims. Otherwise it scans the dirty bitmap from p.offset, wrapping once at sm->last_victim, skipping segments that are invalid (CONFIG_F2FS_CHECK_FS), in use, holding checkpointed data when SBI_CP_DISABLED, already in victim_secmap for BG_GC, or pinned for FG_GC; for age-threshold GC it collects entries with add_victim_entry, else it keeps the lowest get_gc_cost; it stops after p.max_search candidates and updates sm->last_victim. For GC_AT/AT_SSR it then calls lookup_victim_by_age and release_victim_entry and, if nothing was found and the elapsed time is below the age threshold, retries once with the threshold zero. If min_segno is not NULL_SEGNO, *result is set to its unit-aligned segment (got_it); at got_result, with LFS it records the section in sbi->cur_victim_sec for FG_GC or sets its bit in victim_secmap otherwise; ret = 0. When no victim was found ret stays -ENODATA. out: traces the choice if min_segno is not NULL_SEGNO, unlocks and returns ret. Note: when selected via the hint path (got_result) ret is set to 0 and *result is unchanged, and the next_victim_seg path sets *result directly.
note: packet name get_victim_by_type does not exist in gc.c; real function is f2fs_get_victim (gc.c:766-969, slice 780-1038 cut the head, lines 766-779). Mechanical complaint (name not in slice) therefore resolved by renaming.

name: f2fs_recover_inline_data
prose: Precondition: inode is a valid f2fs inode (sbi = F2FS_I_SB(inode)) and nfolio is the recovered node folio from roll-forward recovery (inline.c:294-351). Postcondition: returns an int: 1 when the inline data was recovered from nfolio (line 330), 0 when no inline data needed recovering from nfolio (350), or a negative errno. ri is F2FS_INODE(nfolio) only when nfolio is an inode node, else NULL. Case A, inode has inline data and ri has F2FS_INLINE_DATA: it gets the inode folio (error: returns PTR_ERR at 317), waits for writeback, copies MAX_INLINE_DATA(inode) bytes from nfolio's inline area to the inode folio's, sets FI_INLINE_DATA and FI_DATA_EXIST, marks the folio dirty, puts it and returns 1. Case B, inode has inline data but ri does not (or is NULL): it gets the inode folio (error: PTR_ERR at 336), truncates the inline data (f2fs_truncate_inline_inode(inode, ifolio, 0)), decrements the inline-inode stat, clears FI_INLINE_DATA, puts the folio, and returns 0 at 350. Case C, inode has no inline data but ri has F2FS_INLINE_DATA: it calls f2fs_truncate_blocks(inode, 0, false) (non-zero result returned at 346), increments the inline-inode stat and jumps into case A's block (process_inline) which then copies the data and returns 1 or an error from f2fs_get_inode_folio. Neither flag set: returns 0.
note: slice cut head/tail (function at 294-351). Unreviewed originally; the first reviewer's complaint (omits returns 1, 0, PTR_ERR and the truncate_blocks error) is right and all are now listed (330, 350, 317/336, 346). Contract left empty (pointer parameters).

name: sanity_check_raw_super
prose: Precondition: sbi is an initialised f2fs_sb_info, folio and index identify the superblock page whose raw f2fs_super_block is read through F2FS_SUPER_BLOCK(folio, index) (super.c:3909-4076, static int). Postcondition: returns 0 if every check passes, -EINVAL at 3921 if the magic is not F2FS_SUPER_MAGIC, and -EFSCORRUPTED (with an f2fs_info message) for each other failed check; it modifies nothing. Checks in order: with the SB_CHKSUM feature, checksum_offset must equal offsetof(struct f2fs_super_block, crc) and the stored crc must equal f2fs_crc32 over the first crc_offset bytes; log_blocksize must equal F2FS_BLKSIZE_BITS; log_blocks_per_seg must be 9; log_sectorsize must lie in [F2FS_MIN_LOG_SECTOR_SIZE, F2FS_MAX_LOG_SECTOR_SIZE] and log_sectors_per_block + log_sectorsize must equal F2FS_MAX_LOG_SECTOR_SIZE; segment_count within [F2FS_MIN_SEGMENTS, F2FS_MAX_SEGMENT]; section_count at least 1 and not above segment_count_main, segs_per_sec non-zero and not above segment_count; segment_count_main == section_count * segs_per_sec; segment_count / segs_per_sec >= section_count; segment_count <= block_count >> 9; if RDEV(0).path is set, the sum of total_segments over the listed devices must equal segment_count, otherwise, with the BLKZONED feature the main block device must be zoned; secs_per_zone must be non-zero and not above total sections; extension_count, hot_ext_count and their sum must not exceed F2FS_MAX_EXTENSION; cp_payload must be below blocks_per_seg - F2FS_CP_PACKS - NR_CURSEG_PERSIST_TYPE; node_ino, meta_ino and root_ino must be 1, 2 and 3; finally sanity_check_area_boundary must return false (a true result gives -EFSCORRUPTED at 4073).
note: packet name f2fs_sanity_check_sb does not exist. The described superblock checks are sanity_check_raw_super (super.c:3909-4076); the slice 3924-4197 starts inside it (slice cut head) and also contains f2fs_sanity_check_ckpt (4078 on), which is a different function not listed in this item. No reviewer reason beyond the mechanical name mismatch.

name: f2fs_scan_devices
prose: Precondition: sbi is an f2fs_sb_info being set up at mount time, with raw_super readable through F2FS_RAW_SUPER(sbi) (super.c:4693-4799, static int). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno. If RDEV(0).path is empty and the main block device is not zoned it returns 0 at line 4704 with no change. Otherwise max_devices is MAX_DEVICES, or 1 for a single zoned device; it allocates sbi->devs (-ENOMEM at 4717 if that fails), sets aligned_blksize = true and bggc_io_aware (AWARE_READ_IO under CONFIG_BLK_DEV_ZONED, with max_open_zones and blkzone_alloc_policy set), then loops i over the devices: for a single zoned device it sets FDEV(0) total_segments/start_blk/end_blk from segment_count_main; device 0 uses sb->s_bdev_file, a later device with an empty path ends the loop; in the multi-device case it copies the path and total_segments, sets start_blk and end_blk (device 0 also gets segment0_blkaddr added and sets allocate_section_hint; later devices start at the previous end_blk + 1 and are opened with bdev_file_open_by_path). An error-pointer bdev_file returns PTR_ERR at 4765. It then sets FDEV(i).bdev and sbi->s_ndevs = i + 1 (before the following checks, so devices needing release are counted), clears aligned_blksize if the logical block size differs from the main device, and for a zoned device (CONFIG_BLK_DEV_ZONED) returns -EINVAL at 4778 if the blkzoned feature is off, or -EINVAL at 4782 if init_blkz_info fails, and breaks the loop for the single-zoned-device case. Each device is logged. After the loop it returns 0 at 4798. Failures leave sbi->devs allocated and earlier devices opened (the caller releases them).
note: item was 'unnamed multi-device init loop' (dropped in earlier rounds): the slice 4708-4961 starts inside f2fs_scan_devices (super.c:4693-4799), so per rule 6 it is FIXED under the real name rather than dropped (slice cut head, lines 4693-4707). The slice also continues into following functions which are not part of this item.

name: f2fs_fill_super
prose: Precondition: sb is a super_block whose block device is open and fc is the filesystem context carrying the parsed mount options in fc->fs_private (super.c:4863-5384, static int). Postcondition: returns an int through three return statements: -ENOMEM at 4887 if the f2fs_sb_info allocation fails (nothing else done); 0 at 5294 after a successful mount (sb->s_fs_info = sbi, s_root set, sbi->umount_lock_holder reset to NULL); and 'return err' at 5383 after the failure unwinding. Order of work: allocate and initialise sbi and its locks; set the block size (failure: goto free_sbi with err = -EINVAL); read_raw_super_block; copy the error/stop-reason arrays; default_options, f2fs_check_opt_consistency, f2fs_apply_options, f2fs_sanity_check_options, f2fs_setup_casefold; set sb operations and flags; set SBI_POR_DOING; init write-merge IO, sb info, iostat, percpu info, page array cache; read the meta inode with f2fs_iget; f2fs_get_valid_checkpoint; set flags from the checkpoint; f2fs_scan_devices; f2fs_init_post_read_wq; copy counters from the checkpoint; optionally start the checkpoint thread (not for read-only, DISABLE_CHECKPOINT or without MERGE_CHECKPOINT); build the segment and node managers; f2fs_build_stats; read the node inode and the root inode (the root must be a directory with non-zero i_blocks, i_size and i_nlink, else -EINVAL); d_make_root (-ENOMEM); f2fs_init_compress_inode; f2fs_register_sysfs; with CONFIG_QUOTA enable quotas for a writable quota_ino fs (an error is only logged) and f2fs_recover_quota_begin; f2fs_recover_orphan_inodes (error: free_meta). If CP_DISABLED_FLAG is set in the checkpoint it sets skip_recovery = true and jumps to reset_checkpoint. Roll-forward: when neither DISABLE_ROLL_FORWARD nor NORECOVERY is set: on a read-only device, if the last checkpoint was not a clean umount it runs f2fs_recover_fsync_data(sbi, true) (a positive result becomes -EROFS, any error goes to free_meta) and then goes to reset_checkpoint (recovery skipped); otherwise need_fsck sets SBI_NEED_FSCK, skip_recovery goes to reset_checkpoint, else f2fs_recover_fsync_data(sbi, false) runs and a negative result sets skip_recovery (unless -ENOMEM) and need_fsck and goes to free_meta. When roll-forward is disabled it only checks (recover_fsync_data(sbi, true)): a positive result is -EINVAL and free_meta for a writable mount, or is dropped (err = 0) for read-only. reset_checkpoint: f2fs_recover_quota_end; if skip_recovery it calls f2fs_check_and_fix_write_pointer; a non-zero err goes to free_meta; it clears SBI_POR_DOING, f2fs_init_inmem_curseg, disables/enables checkpointing as the options and flags say, starts the GC thread for a writable mount with background GC on or GC_MERGE (errors go to sync_free_meta), commits the superblock if a backup superblock was used (its result is only logged), joins the shrinker, tunes parameters and returns 0. Failure unwinding: sync_free_meta syncs the filesystem and sets retry_cnt = 0; free_meta, free_compress_inode, free_root_inode, free_node_inode, free_stats, free_nm, free_sm, stop_ckpt_thread, free_devices, free_meta_inode, free_page_array_cache, free_percpu, free_iostat, free_bio_info, free_options, free_sb_buf and free_sbi release progressively earlier stages in that order (each label falls through to the next), and finally sbi is freed and sb->s_fs_info cleared. If retry_cnt > 0 and skip_recovery is set, the whole mount is retried once: retry_cnt-- , shrink_dcache_sb(sb) and goto try_onemore (which reallocates sbi and rereads everything); otherwise it returns err.
note: slice cut head and tail (function at 4863-5384, slice 4962-5233). reviewer round 15 right in substance: skip_recovery at 5208-5209 jumps to reset_checkpoint (not a retry); the whole-mount retry is the separate try_onemore at 5378-5381 after unwinding, taken only when retry_cnt > 0 and skip_recovery is true (skip_recovery is set at 5178 or 5214), and sync_free_meta clears retry_cnt (5299) so retry is not taken after a post-recovery failure.

name: f2fs_parse_param
prose: Precondition: fc is an fs_context whose fs_private points to an initialised struct f2fs_fs_context and param is one mount parameter (super.c:741-1191, static int). Postcondition: returns 0 when the parameter was accepted (including options that are only logged as unsupported or deprecated) and a negative errno otherwise; it only records the choice in ctx (option bits via ctx_set_opt/ctx_clear_opt, values in F2FS_CTX_INFO(ctx), and ctx->spec_mask bits) and does not change the mounted filesystem. The two return points of the function body are 'return token' at 756 (fs_parse failed: its negative result) and 'return 0' at 1190; the other returns are inside the switch (token): -EINVAL for inline_xattr_size outside [MIN_INLINE_XATTR_SIZE, MAX_INLINE_XATTR_SIZE] (798, with CONFIG_F2FS_FS_XATTR), for active_logs not 2, 4 or NR_CURSEG_PERSIST_TYPE (826), for fault_type above BIT(FAULT_MAX) (900, with CONFIG_F2FS_FAULT_INJECTION), for compress_log_size outside [MIN_COMPRESS_LOG_SIZE, MAX_COMPRESS_LOG_SIZE] (1091), for an unknown compress_algorithm name (1084), and for an over-long or too many compress/nocompress extensions (1104, 1124); the helper results returned unchanged for jquota names (f2fs_note_qf_name/f2fs_unnote_qf_name, 942/950/958) and for test_dummy_encryption (986); the strscpy negative result for an extension copy (1112, 1132); inside checkpoint= (which is re-parsed with match_token), -EINVAL for a bad match_int, a percentage outside 0-100 and an unknown sub-option (1008-1033). For compress_algorithm=lz4... or zstd..., a non-zero result from f2fs_set_lz4hc_level or f2fs_set_zstd_level is returned as -EINVAL, not as the helper's own value (1058, 1068); lzo and lzo-rle set the algorithm and level 0; an algorithm not compiled in only logs a message and returns 0. Options requiring unavailable kernel configuration (xattr, ACL, fault injection, quota, compression, inline crypt) are logged with f2fs_info and accepted. Boolean options use result.negated to set or clear the corresponding bit; a duplicate compress extension already present is silently accepted without adding it (1107-1108, 1127-1128).
note: slice cut head and tail (function at 741-1191, slice 816-1100). reviewer round 15 right: super.c:1056-1058 and 1066-1068 return -EINVAL, not the helper's return value.

name: f2fs_init_sysfs
prose: Precondition: the global kset f2fs_kset and kobjects f2fs_feat and f2fs_tune are unregistered and f2fs_proc_root is not yet created; called once at module init (sysfs.c:1929-1964, __init, no parameters). Postcondition: returns 0 on success, with f2fs_kset registered under fs_kobj as 'f2fs', f2fs_feat added as 'features', f2fs_tune added as 'tuning' (both with parent NULL, i.e. under the kset's directory as the kobjects' default parent) and f2fs_proc_root = proc_mkdir("fs/f2fs", NULL). On failure it returns a negative errno ret: if kset_register fails it returns ret at line 1937 immediately, having done nothing else (no kset_unregister); if kobject_init_and_add of f2fs_feat fails it jumps to unregister_kset, which calls kset_unregister(&f2fs_kset) and returns ret, without a kobject_put of f2fs_feat; if kobject_init_and_add of f2fs_tune fails it does kobject_put(&f2fs_feat) and kset_unregister (not kobject_put of f2fs_tune); if proc_mkdir returns NULL it sets ret = -ENOMEM and does kobject_put(&f2fs_tune), kobject_put(&f2fs_feat) and kset_unregister(&f2fs_kset), then returns ret (1963).
note: slice does not start at the function (function at 1929-1964, slice 1775-2040 includes it). reviewers all right: round 1 (no kobject_put of f2fs_feat when its kobject_init_and_add fails, sysfs.c:1941-1942 jumps past put_feat), round 2 and round 15 (kset_register failure returns at 1936-1937 doing nothing). Contract left empty (global state).

name: writeback_inode
prose: Precondition: inode is a valid FAT inode with a valid i_mapping (inode.c:1865-1878, static int). Postcondition: has one return, 'return ret' at 1877. It calls sync_inode_metadata(inode, 0), which writes the inode's metadata without waiting for the I/O to complete (wait = 0); if that returns non-zero the value is returned and the data pages are not written. Otherwise it returns the result of filemap_fdatawrite(inode->i_mapping), which starts writeback of the dirty data pages in WB_SYNC_ALL mode (so it may wait for pages already under writeback before rewriting them) but does not wait for the newly started data I/O to finish. The result is 0 or a negative errno from either call; an error from filemap_fdatawrite can be returned after the metadata sync has succeeded.
note: slice cut (function at 1865-1878, slice 1815-1983 includes it). reviewers: original right (filemap_fdatawrite error returned after metadata success, 1876-1877). round 2 right (wait=0 passed to sync_inode_metadata, 1874). round 15 half right: the source comment (1870-1873) is about sync_inode_metadata and data blocks, and filemap_fdatawrite is WB_SYNC_ALL, so 'neither call waits for in-flight I/O' was too strong; stated carefully above (I did not read write_cache_pages in this pass, only rely on known WB_SYNC_ALL behaviour).

name: do_fcntl
prose: Precondition: fd is an open file descriptor whose struct file is filp, cmd is a fcntl command and arg its argument (fcntl.c:447-560, static long). Postcondition: dispatches on cmd and returns the value computed by the matching helper in err, which starts as -EINVAL (so an unknown cmd returns -EINVAL at 559). The three direct early returns are -EFAULT at 487 and 490 (F_GETLK/F_OFD_GETLK: copy_from_user of the flock struct, or copy_to_user of the result after a successful fcntl_getlk) and -EFAULT at 501 (F_SETLK/F_SETLKW/F_OFD_SETLK/F_OFD_SETLKW: copy_from_user failed). Per command: F_CREATED_QUERY, F_DUPFD, F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC, F_DUPFD_QUERY, F_SETFL, F_SETOWN (f_setown with force 1), F_GETOWN_EX, F_SETOWN_EX, F_GETOWNER_UIDS, F_GETSIG, F_SETSIG, F_GETLEASE, F_SETLEASE, F_NOTIFY, F_SETPIPE_SZ/F_GETPIPE_SZ (pipe_fcntl), F_ADD_SEALS/F_GET_SEALS (memfd_fcntl), F_GET_RW_HINT and F_SET_RW_HINT return their helper's result. F_GETFD returns FD_CLOEXEC or 0 from get_close_on_exec(fd); F_SETFD sets the close-on-exec flag from argi & FD_CLOEXEC and returns 0; F_GETFL returns filp->f_flags; F_GETOWN returns f_getown(filp) (a pid, 0 if no owner, or a negative value for a process group; force_successful_syscall_return() is called so that a negative value is not turned into an errno). F_GETSIG returns f_owner_sig(filp, 0, false), which is the stored signal number, or 0 when the file has no f_owner (not -EINVAL). F_GETOWNER_UIDS returns 0 or the put_user error when CONFIG_CHECKPOINT_RESTORE is set; without it fcntl.c:329-334 provides a stub returning -EINVAL. On 64-bit kernels F_OFD_GETLK, F_OFD_SETLK and F_OFD_SETLKW share the lock cases; on 32-bit kernels they are handled in fcntl64. Locks are taken by the helpers, not by do_fcntl itself.
note: slice cut head (function at 447-560, slice 257-557 spans earlier helpers). reviewers: original right (F_GETOWN can return a negative pid as a successful result, fcntl.c:508-513); round 2 right (f_owner_sig returns 0 when there is no f_owner, 442-444); round 15 right (the !CONFIG_CHECKPOINT_RESTORE stub for f_getowner_uids returns -EINVAL, fcntl.c:329-334).

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(dup3, unsigned int, oldfd, unsigned int, newfd, int, flags)
prose: Generated system call dup3(oldfd, newfd, flags) (file.c:1433-1436): its only statement is 'return ksys_dup3(oldfd, newfd, flags)'. ksys_dup3 (file.c:1399-1431) returns -EINVAL if flags has any bit other than O_CLOEXEC or if oldfd == newfd, -EBADF if newfd is at or above RLIMIT_NOFILE; otherwise it takes files->file_lock, calls expand_files(files, newfd) and looks oldfd up; if oldfd is not open it returns -EBADF (after unlocking), if expand_files failed with -EMFILE it returns -EBADF, and with any other negative result it returns that error (lock released each time). Otherwise it returns do_dup2(files, file, newfd, flags), which (file.c:1265-1316, entered with the lock held and releasing it) returns -EBUSY if the newfd slot is reserved but not yet populated, else takes a reference on the file, installs it in newfd (close-on-exec set from flags & O_CLOEXEC), closes the file previously in newfd with filp_close if there was one, and returns newfd.
note: macro-generated: the C function is generated by SYSCALL_DEFINEn (packet names SYSCALL_dupN are not text in the file); name set to the exact macro head at file.c. Unreviewed originally; rewritten from the source lines cited.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE2(dup2, unsigned int, oldfd, unsigned int, newfd)
prose: Generated system call dup2(oldfd, newfd) (file.c:1438-1455). If newfd == oldfd it does not call ksys_dup3: under rcu_read_lock it looks oldfd up with __fget_files_rcu and returns oldfd if it is open (dropping the temporary reference with fput) or -EBADF if it is not (line 1452). Otherwise it returns ksys_dup3(oldfd, newfd, 0): -EBADF if newfd is at or above RLIMIT_NOFILE or oldfd is not open (or if expand_files returns -EMFILE), another negative expand_files error as is, -EBUSY if the target slot is reserved but unpopulated, else newfd after installing a new reference to the file in newfd (without close-on-exec) and closing whatever file was previously there.
note: macro-generated: the C function is generated by SYSCALL_DEFINEn (packet names SYSCALL_dupN are not text in the file); name set to the exact macro head at file.c. Unreviewed originally; rewritten from the source lines cited.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE1(dup, unsigned int, fildes)
prose: Generated system call dup(fildes) (file.c:1457-1470). It takes a reference on the file for fildes with fget_raw (which accepts O_PATH files); if fildes is not open it returns -EBADF. Otherwise it calls get_unused_fd_flags(0): on a non-negative result that fd is the return value and the file is installed in it with fd_install (the reference from fget_raw becomes the descriptor's reference); on a negative result (for example -EMFILE) the reference is dropped with fput and that error is returned.
note: macro-generated: the C function is generated by SYSCALL_DEFINEn (packet names SYSCALL_dupN are not text in the file); name set to the exact macro head at file.c. Unreviewed originally; rewritten from the source lines cited.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(sysfs, int, option, unsigned long, arg1, unsigned long, arg2)
prose: Generated system call sysfs(option, arg1, arg2) (filesystems.c:195-213), compiled only with CONFIG_SYSFS_SYSCALL. Postcondition: returns retval, which starts as -EINVAL, so any option other than 1, 2 or 3 returns -EINVAL. Option 1 returns fs_index(arg1 as a user string): getname error as a negative value, otherwise the zero-based position of the registered filesystem type whose name equals the string (read-lock file_systems_lock around the search; a non-negative result, which can be positive), or -EINVAL if none matches. Option 2 returns fs_name(arg1, arg2): it finds the type at position arg1 (-EINVAL if there is none or try_module_get on its owner fails), then copies its NUL-terminated name to the user buffer arg2 (-EFAULT if copy_to_user fails, else 0) and drops the module reference with put_filesystem; the length of the buffer is not checked. Option 3 returns fs_maxindex(), the number of registered filesystem types (counted under read_lock(&file_systems_lock)). The earlier reviewers were right that the result for option 1 can be positive and that option-1 behaviour needs a statement; no lock is held on return.
note: macro-generated: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(sysfs, ...) at filesystems.c:195 (packet name 'sysfs'). Checked fs_index (132-154), fs_name (156-178), fs_maxindex (180-190). Reviewers original and round 2 right (option 1 can return a positive index, 146-148). Contract left empty (global list).

name: vxfs_bmap1
prose: Precondition: ip is a VxFS inode whose VXFS_INO(ip) info has an organisation type (vii_orgtype), and iblock is the logical file block to map (vxfs_bmap.c:250-272, returns daddr_t, defined as 'daddr_t vxfs_bmap1(struct inode *ip, long iblock)'; the name vxfs_bmap in the packet does not exist). Postcondition: if the orgtype is ext4 (VXFS_ISEXT4) it returns vxfs_bmap_ext4(ip, iblock) (line 256); if typed (VXFS_ISTYPED) it returns vxfs_bmap_typed(ip, iblock) (258); if the orgtype is none or immediate it prints a warning 'unsupported orgtype' and returns 0 (271); for any other orgtype it prints 'has no valid orgtype' and calls BUG() (266), so it does not return normally in that case. name: __mark_inode_dirty
prose: Precondition: inode is a valid inode with a live superblock; flags is a combination of I_DIRTY_SYNC, I_DIRTY_DATASYNC, I_DIRTY_PAGES and I_DIRTY_TIME (I_DIRTY_TIME is not expected together with I_DIRTY_PAGES, WARN_ON_ONCE); the caller does not hold inode->i_lock (fs-writeback.c:2579-2716, returns void). Postcondition: returns nothing. If flags has I_DIRTY_INODE bits: when inode->i_state has I_DIRTY_TIME it is cleared under i_lock and I_DIRTY_TIME is added to flags (also when the inode was already dirty, so the I_DIRTY_TIME bit of i_state can change even if nothing else does); then sb->s_op->dirty_inode(inode, flags & (I_DIRTY_INODE|I_DIRTY_TIME)) is called only if the superblock has that callback, and I_DIRTY_TIME is then removed from flags. Otherwise dirtytime = flags & I_DIRTY_TIME. After an smp_mb(), if inode->i_state already contains all the bits in flags it returns at line 2634 without taking i_lock. Otherwise under i_lock, if the bits are still missing: it records was_dirty = i_state & I_DIRTY, attaches a writeback context (inode_attach_wb), sets the flag bits, and if the inode was not dirty it takes the wb list lock (locked_inode_to_wb_and_lock_list, which releases and retakes i_lock). It then does not queue the inode (goto out_unlock) when I_SYNC_QUEUED is set, when the inode is not a block device and is unhashed, or when I_FREEING is set; in those cases only i_state was updated. When the inode was already dirty (was_dirty) the list position is not changed. When it was newly dirty and is queued: dirtied_when (and dirtied_time_when for dirty-time) is set to jiffies, the inode is moved to wb->b_dirty if now I_DIRTY or b_dirty_time otherwise, the delayed wakeup of the bdi writeback thread is requested if this is the first dirty inode for a writeback-capable bdi, both locks are released and it returns (2709). out_unlock releases the wb list lock if held and i_lock and returns (end of function).
note: slice cut head and tail (function at 2579-2716, slice 2585-2852). reviewers: original right (I_SYNC_QUEUED case does not add the newly dirty inode to a wb list, 2661-2662); round 2 right (dirty_inode callback only if sb->s_op->dirty_inode, 2610); round 15 right (2593-2598 clear I_DIRTY_TIME even when I_DIRTY_INODE already set).

name: fuse_update_get_attr
prose: Precondition: inode is a FUSE inode, idmap is the mount idmap used when filling a kstat, file may be NULL, stat may be NULL, request_mask and flags are the statx request mask and AT_STATX_* flags (dir.c:1337-1391, static int). Postcondition: single return 'return err' at 1390; err is 0 or a negative errno. request_mask is first reduced to STATX_BASIC_STATS | STATX_BTIME (and to STATX_BASIC_STATS if fc->no_statx). It decides sync: false when the mask is empty, true for AT_STATX_FORCE_SYNC, false for AT_STATX_DONT_SYNC, true if some requested attribute is both invalidated (fi->inval_mask) and not covered by the cache mask, otherwise true only when fi->i_time is in the past. If sync it drops cached ACLs and asks the server: with STATX_BTIME requested and statx supported it calls fuse_do_statx (-ENOSYS: sets fc->no_statx, clears err and retries once from the top without statx), otherwise fuse_do_getattr; err is that call's result. Those helpers return -EIO (and mark the inode bad with fuse_make_bad) when the server returns invalid attributes or an inode type that does not match (fuse_do_getattr 1322-1325, fuse_do_statx 1267-1271), as well as any error from the request itself. If no sync is needed and stat is non-NULL, it fills stat from the cached inode with generic_fillattr, then overrides mode, ino and blksize from the stored originals, and adds the cached btime if FUSE_I_BTIME is set; if stat is NULL and no sync is needed nothing is filled. With sync, stat is filled by the helper only on success and only if stat is non-NULL.
note: slice cut head (function at 1337-1391, slice 1288-1540). reviewers: original right (stat can be NULL, 1379/1330/1280, and success does not fill stat then). round 2 right: the idmap is used in generic_fillattr (1380) and passed to the helpers, it is not 'may be NULL' in the sense claimed. round 15 right: -EIO via fuse_do_getattr/fuse_do_statx for bad attributes or wrong inode type, which also call fuse_make_bad.

name: fuse_file_read_iter
prose: Precondition: iocb->ki_filp is an open FUSE file whose private_data is its struct fuse_file, to describes the read destination (file.c:1778-1797, static ssize_t). Postcondition: each branch is a tail call and the function has these return points: -EIO at 1785 if the inode is marked bad (fuse_is_bad); fuse_dax_read_iter(iocb, to) at 1788 if the inode is a DAX inode (checked before the direct-IO flag); otherwise, if ff->open_flags has FOPEN_DIRECT_IO, fuse_direct_read_iter(iocb, to) (1792; this takes precedence over passthrough); else if the file is in passthrough mode (fuse_file_passthrough(ff)), fuse_passthrough_read_iter(iocb, to) (1794); else fuse_cache_read_iter(iocb, to) (1796). The return value is that of the chosen routine (bytes read or a negative errno); the function itself takes no lock.

name: gfs2_trans_add_meta
prose: Precondition: current->journal_info points to the running gfs2 transaction tr, gl is the glock owning the metadata buffer bh, and bh is a metadata buffer of the filesystem (trans.c:250-313, returns void). Postcondition: returns nothing. It locks the buffer (lock_buffer). If the buffer is already pinned it sets TR_TOUCHED in tr->tr_flags and goes to out (no list changes). Otherwise it takes the log lock; if bh->b_private (the gfs2_bufdata) is NULL it drops the log lock and buffer lock, takes the folio lock, allocates bd with gfs2_alloc_bufdata unless another task attached one meanwhile, and re-takes the buffer and log locks. It asserts bd->bd_gl == gl and sets TR_TOUCHED; if bd->bd_list is non-empty (already in a transaction list) it goes to out_unlock without further changes. Otherwise it sets GLF_LFLUSH and GLF_DIRTY on the glock (before the checks that follow, so this happens even on the exits below), checks that the block's meta header magic is GFS2_MAGIC (else logs 'Attempting to add uninitialised block to journal' and BUG()), and if the filesystem is withdrawn logs and goes to out_unlock, adding nothing to the transaction; if the superblock is frozen (SB_FREEZE_COMPLETE) it logs, sets withdraw = true and goes to out_unlock. On the normal path it pins the buffer (gfs2_pin), clears mh->__pad0, sets mh_jid to the journal id, adds bd to tr->tr_buf and increments tr->tr_num_buf_new. out_unlock drops the log lock and, if withdraw is set, calls gfs2_assert_withdraw(sdp, 0); out unlocks the buffer.
note: packet name gfs2_trans_add_buffer does not exist in trans.c; the slice 253-357 is the body of gfs2_trans_add_meta (250-313, slice cut head). reviewer round 15 right: GLF_LFLUSH and GLF_DIRTY are set at trans.c:283-284 before the withdrawn exit at 292-296, so 'nothing else changes' on the withdrawn path was false.

name: hfs_btree_inc_height
prose: Precondition: tree is a valid HFS B-tree held by the caller (the function is called under the tree's usual serialisation, e.g. from hfs_brec_insert); tree->root is 0 for an empty tree or the cnid of the current root node (hfs/brec.c:477-548, static int). The packet name hfs_btree_new_root does not exist; this is hfs_btree_inc_height. Postcondition: returns an int via three return statements: PTR_ERR(node) at 488 if the current root cannot be read (hfs_bnode_find on tree->root fails; nothing else changed), PTR_ERR(new_node) at 493 if hfs_bmap_alloc fails (after hfs_bnode_put(node) of the old root, no tree fields changed), and 0 at 547. On success: tree->root is set to the new node, and if the tree had depth 0 the new node becomes the only leaf (leaf_head = leaf_tail = new node, type HFS_NODE_LEAF, 0 records), otherwise the new node is an HFS_NODE_INDEX node with 1 record; the new node's parent, next and prev are 0, its height is ++tree->depth; its node descriptor is written to the node, and with an old root, the old root's parent is set to the new root and an index record (a copy of the old root's first key, with key size taken from the key length byte for leaf nodes or variable-index-key trees, else from tree->max_key_len + 1, followed by the old root's node number) is written into the new node together with its record offset; the old root node reference and then the new node reference are dropped (hfs_bnode_put), and mark_inode_dirty(tree->inode) is called.
note: item was marked dropped as 'not in slice' but the slice 510-548 is the tail of hfs_btree_inc_height (brec.c:477-548; slice cut head). Per rule 6 FIXED under the real name hfs_btree_inc_height. The earlier prose said 'new root has already been allocated', which is wrong: the function allocates it itself (hfs_bmap_alloc at 490).

name: hfsplus_compare_dentry
prose: Precondition: dentry belongs to a mounted HFS+ filesystem, str points to len bytes of the first name, name is the qstr of the second name (unicode.c:481-565, int hfsplus_compare_dentry(const struct dentry *dentry, unsigned int len, const char *str, const struct qstr *name); the packet name dstr_compare_fragment does not exist). Postcondition: returns -1, 1 or 0, comparing the two names in HFS+ filename order; it modifies nothing. casefold is true unless HFSPLUS_SB_CASEFOLD is clear and decompose is true unless HFSPLUS_SB_NODECOMPOSE is set (both read from the superblock flags). The loop runs while both names have unread input bytes: when a side has no pending decomposed characters it converts the next character (asc2unichar), decomposing it when decompose is set (Hangul decomposition buffers), otherwise treating it as a single unit; then it compares the current units, applying case_fold when casefold is set, and a unit whose case-fold value is 0 is skipped on that side (continue) without comparing. The first unequal pair returns -1 if the first unit is smaller or 1 if larger. When the loop ends it returns -1 if the remaining input length of the first name is smaller than that of the second (len1 < len2), 1 if larger, else 0; units still pending from an earlier decomposition (dsize1/dsize2) are not examined at that point.
note: item was 'dstr_compare_fragment' (not a function in the file); the slice 533-565 is the tail of hfsplus_compare_dentry (unicode.c:481-565, slice cut head). Fixed under the real name. Earlier prose (shorter fragment that is a prefix is less) was imprecise: the final comparison is on remaining input byte counts (560-563) and ignores pending decomposed units.

name: jbd2_journal_commit_transaction
prose: Precondition: journal is a jbd2 journal with journal->j_running_transaction non-NULL and journal->j_committing_transaction NULL (both J_ASSERTed); the caller (the commit thread) does not hold journal->j_state_lock (jbd2/commit.c:348-1160, void, no return statements: it ends at the closing brace). Postcondition: the running transaction has been written to the log (or the journal aborted), moved through the states T_LOCKED, T_SWITCH, T_FLUSH, T_COMMIT, T_COMMIT_DFLUSH, T_COMMIT_JFLUSH, T_COMMIT_CALLBACK and T_FINISHED, journal->j_commit_sequence set to its tid, journal->j_committing_transaction set to NULL, the commit callbacks called and waiters woken; I/O errors do not make it return an error but call jbd2_journal_abort. Steps: if JBD2_FLUSHED is set it updates the superblock log tail under j_checkpoint_mutex. Under j_state_lock it sets JBD2_FULL_COMMIT_ONGOING, waits (uninterruptibly, dropping and retaking the lock) while JBD2_FAST_COMMIT_ONGOING is set, then sets the transaction T_LOCKED, waits for outstanding updates (jbd2_journal_wait_updates), sets T_SWITCH and refiles all buffers on t_reserved_list (freeing undo-committed data), then outside the lock cleans the checkpoint list, clears revoked flags and switches the revoke table. It subtracts the reserved credits, sets T_FLUSH and makes it the committing transaction (j_running_transaction = NULL), submits data buffers (journal_submit_data_buffers; an error aborts the journal), writes revoke records and sets T_COMMIT. It then loops over t_buffers: if the journal is aborted each buffer is un-journalled and refiled (jumping to start_journal_io when the last one goes); otherwise it obtains a descriptor block (jbd2_journal_get_descriptor_buffer; failure aborts with -EIO and continues), maps the next log block (jbd2_journal_next_log_block; failure aborts the journal and continues), writes a shadow copy of the metadata with jbd2_journal_write_metadata_buffer, records a tag, and when the descriptor is full, the wbuf is full or no buffers remain it marks the last tag and submits all buffers (start_journal_io: descriptor checksum, optional crc32 of data, lock_buffer/submit_bh). Afterwards it calls journal_finish_inode_data_buffers (an error is only logged and cleared), gets the journal tail (update_tail, cleared unless enough space would be freed), sets T_COMMIT_DFLUSH, flushes the filesystem device when it is separate from the journal device and a data flush or tail update is needed and barriers are on, and with the async_commit feature submits the commit record early (error: abort). It finishes the plug and waits for all log buffers on io_bufs (each wait sets err = -EIO if not uptodate, refiles the shadowed buffer to BJ_Forget and frees the temporary buffer head) and then on log_bufs; a non-zero err aborts the journal. It sets T_COMMIT_JFLUSH, submits the commit record unless async_commit (an error aborts), waits for the commit record (cbh) taking its result as err, issues a flush of the journal device for async_commit with barriers, aborts on err, and updates the log tail if update_tail is set. At restart_loop it processes t_forget under j_list_lock, releasing frozen/committed data, removing from the old checkpoint transaction, inserting still-dirty buffers into this transaction's checkpoint list (clearing jbddirty when the journal is aborted), handling freed buffers, and refiling or freeing each; it then retakes j_state_lock and j_list_lock and if t_forget has become non-empty drops the locks and does goto restart_loop. It then links the transaction into journal->j_checkpoint_transactions, sets T_COMMIT_CALLBACK, publishes j_commit_sequence, clears j_committing_transaction, updates j_average_commit_time, drops the lock and calls j_commit_callback and j_fc_cleanup_callback if set, clears JBD2_FULL_COMMIT_ONGOING and JBD2_FAST_COMMIT_ONGOING, sets T_FINISHED and, if the checkpoint list is empty, drops and frees the transaction, wakes j_wait_done_commit and j_fc_wait, and adds the statistics under j_history_lock.
note: item was 'journal_commit_transaction' (dropped / still-rejected as not-in-slice); the real function is jbd2_journal_commit_transaction at jbd2/commit.c:348-1160 and both packet slices (515-769 and 770-1062) are middle pieces of it (slice cut head and tail), so per rule 6 FIXED under the real name. The two records are two slices of the same function, so both carry the same whole-function prose (only one should be used when both are ingested).

name: __jbd2_log_start_commit
prose: Precondition: journal is a valid journal and the caller holds journal->j_state_lock for writing (it is called under that lock, journal.c:445-480, static int). Postcondition: returns 0 at line 449 if journal->j_commit_request already equals target (nothing changed). If the running transaction exists and its t_tid equals target, it sets j_commit_request = target, records t_requested = jiffies, wakes j_wait_commit (the commit is done by the commit thread, not here) and returns 1 (469). Otherwise (the target is an older, no longer running transaction, or there is no running one) it returns 0 at 479, first issuing a WARN_ONCE if j_commit_request is not at or after target; no state changes in that case.
note: slice shows neighbouring functions (slice 257-512 starts at jbd2_journal_start_thread); function located at the lines cited. Unreviewed originally; rewritten from the source.

name: jbd2_log_start_commit
prose: Precondition: journal is a valid initialised journal and tid a transaction id; the caller must not hold j_state_lock (journal.c:482-490). Postcondition: takes journal->j_state_lock for writing, returns the result of __jbd2_log_start_commit(journal, tid) (1 if a commit of the running transaction tid was newly requested and the commit thread woken, otherwise 0) after releasing the lock; it does not wait for the commit.
note: slice shows neighbouring functions (slice 257-512 starts at jbd2_journal_start_thread); function located at the lines cited. Unreviewed originally; rewritten from the source.

name: __jbd2_journal_force_commit
prose: Precondition: journal is a valid initialised journal and the caller does not hold j_state_lock (journal.c:499-527, static int). Postcondition: returns an int with these return points: 0 at 516 when there is nothing to commit (no running transaction usable and no committing transaction); otherwise ret at 526. Under the read lock it picks the running transaction only if the current task has no active handle (current->journal_info is NULL), and records need_to_start if its tid is not yet covered by j_commit_request; else it picks the committing transaction. If it picked one it releases the lock, calls jbd2_log_start_commit(journal, tid) when need_to_start, and waits with jbd2_log_wait_commit(journal, tid), whose result is 0 normally or -EIO if the journal was aborted. A zero result becomes 1; a negative result is returned as is. So the return is 0 (nothing to commit), 1 (committed) or a negative error (-EIO), as the function comment at 492-497 says.
note: slice shows neighbouring functions (slice 257-512 starts at jbd2_journal_start_thread); function located at the lines cited. Unreviewed originally; rewritten from the source. reviewer round 1 right: the function can return a negative value (jbd2_log_wait_commit returns -EIO for an aborted journal, journal.c:689-691).

name: do_one_pass
prose: Precondition: journal is an initialised journal whose superblock gives the starting sequence (s_sequence) and log block (s_start); info is the recovery_info being filled or consumed; pass is PASS_SCAN, PASS_REVOKE or PASS_REPLAY (recovery.c:588-950, static int). Postcondition: returns success (0 or a negative errno) at line 945, or err at 949 after label failed (brelse of the buffer first). Setup: next_commit_ID and next_log_block come from the superblock; in PASS_SCAN info->start_transaction is set to the first id; in PASS_REVOKE, when info->nr_revokes is above JOURNAL_REVOKE_DEFAULT_HASH * 16 a larger revoke table is allocated (on failure it falls back to the default table with a message). Main loop (while 1): for non-scan passes it stops (break) when next_commit_ID has reached info->end_transaction; it reads the block at next_log_block with jread (error: goto failed returning that error), advances and wraps; it breaks out of the loop if the block lacks the JBD2 magic or its sequence is not next_commit_ID. Then by block type: JBD2_DESCRIPTOR_BLOCK: if the descriptor checksum is bad, in a non-scan pass it fails with -EFSBADCRC, in PASS_SCAN it only sets need_check_commit_time; in non-replay passes it skips over the tags (in PASS_SCAN with the checksum feature and while info->end_transaction is not yet set it calls calc_chksums instead, breaking out of the loop if that returns non-zero); in PASS_REPLAY it calls jbd2_do_replay, a -ENOMEM result goes to failed and any other error is remembered in success while the scan continues. JBD2_COMMIT_BLOCK: in non-scan passes it just increments next_commit_ID; in PASS_SCAN it reads the commit time and, if need_check_commit_time is set, fails with -EFSBADCRC when commit_time >= the last transaction's, otherwise ends the scan successfully (ignore_crc_mismatch then done); with the checksum feature it first breaks out of the loop (setting journal->j_failed_commit) if info->end_transaction is already set, and otherwise verifies the crc32 (mismatch goes to chksum_error); without that feature it verifies the commit block checksum or a partial one (chksum_ok); at chksum_error it ignores the mismatch if commit_time is older than the last one, else sets info->end_transaction and head_block and, without the async_commit feature, sets j_failed_commit and breaks, with async_commit it falls through; chksum_ok records last_trans_commit_time, head_block = next_log_block and advances next_commit_ID. JBD2_REVOKE_BLOCK: skipped unless the pass is REVOKE or SCAN; in PASS_SCAN a bad checksum sets need_check_commit_time; scan_revoke_records errors go to failed. Any other block type goes to done. At done: brelse; in PASS_SCAN it sets info->end_transaction and info->head_block if still unset; in other passes, if info->end_transaction differs from next_commit_ID it logs an error and sets success = -EIO unless success is already non-zero; with the fast-commit feature and a pass other than PASS_REVOKE it calls fc_do_one_pass, whose error replaces success; it returns success.
note: slice cut head (function at 588-950, slice 758-996). reviewer round 15 right: the break on info->end_transaction already set (recovery.c:832-836) occurs only inside the jbd2_has_feature_checksum branch (826-851).

name: jbd2_journal_dirty_metadata
prose: Precondition: handle is the caller's active handle, bh is a buffer that has been given write access in this handle's transaction (it has a journal head); the caller holds no jh->b_state_lock (transaction.c:1490-1644). Postcondition: returns an int with a single exit 'return ret' at 1643 except for the first check: -EUCLEAN at 1498 if buffer_jbd(bh) is false. Otherwise: if jh->b_modified is already 1 it only checks (asserting under b_state_lock) that a buffer in this transaction is on the BJ_Metadata list and returns 0 without further changes. Otherwise it takes jh->b_state_lock: if the handle is aborted it returns -EROFS (1550); if jh->b_modified == 0 it needs at least one buffer credit in the handle, else -ENOSPC (WARN_ON_ONCE), and sets b_modified = 1 and decrements handle->h_total_credits; fast path: if the buffer is already on this transaction's BJ_Metadata list it returns 0 without calling set_buffer_jbddirty (but -EINVAL, with a log message, if that transaction is not the journal's running transaction, 1591); otherwise it calls set_buffer_jbddirty(bh); if jh->b_transaction is a different transaction it is expected to be the committing transaction with b_next_transaction equal to this one: in that case the buffer is left for the commit to refile and returns 0, and any other state gives a message, WARN_ON and -EINVAL; if jh->b_transaction is this transaction (not yet BJ_Metadata), it asserts b_frozen_data is NULL and files the buffer on the BJ_Metadata list under j_list_lock. The state lock is released and ret returned.

name: __jffs2_dbg_dump_node
prose: Precondition: c is a valid jffs2_sb_info with a readable flash device and ofs a flash offset (debug.c:772-865, void; compiled only when JFFS2_DBG_DUMPS or JFFS2_DBG_PARANOIA_CHECKS is enabled; the name in the packet lacked the leading underscores). Postcondition: returns nothing and changes no filesystem state; it only prints. It prints the offset, then reads sizeof(union jffs2_node_union) bytes at ofs with jffs2_flash_read; if the read fails or returns a short count it logs an error and returns (line 787). It prints the common header (magic, nodetype, totlen, hdr_crc); if the crc32 over the first sizeof(node.u) - 4 bytes differs from hdr_crc it logs 'wrong common header CRC' and returns (798); if the magic is neither JFFS2_MAGIC_BITMASK nor JFFS2_OLD_MAGIC_BITMASK it logs and returns (806). Then by nodetype: JFFS2_NODETYPE_INODE prints the inode fields and checks the crc32 over sizeof(node.i) - 8 bytes against node_crc (mismatch: logs 'wrong node header CRC' and returns, 835); JFFS2_NODETYPE_DIRENT prints the dirent fields, writes a NUL at node.d.name[node.d.nsize] in the local copy, prints the name, and checks the crc32 over sizeof(node.d) - 8 bytes against node_crc (mismatch: logs and returns, 857); any other type prints 'node type is unknown'. All paths end by returning (falling off the end at 865).
note: item name in packet was jffs2_dbg_dump_node (does not exist, real name __jffs2_dbg_dump_node at debug.c:773); the slice 781-866 is its body (slice cut head). Reviewers' only complaint was mechanical.

name: jffs2_mark_node_obsolete
prose: Precondition: c is the jffs2 superblock info and ref is a raw node reference (or NULL); the caller does not hold c->erase_free_sem or c->erase_completion_lock (the function takes them itself) (jffs2/nodemgmt.c:586-842, void). Postcondition: returns nothing. Returns early without any change: if ref is NULL (logs a notice, line 598); if ref is already obsolete (603). If ref->flash_offset is beyond the last erase block it logs and BUG()s (608). It takes c->erase_free_sem only if jffs2_can_mark_obsolete(c) and the filesystem is not read-only and neither JFFS2_SB_FLAG_SCANNING nor JFFS2_SB_FLAG_BUILDING is set. Under c->erase_completion_lock it reduces the used size (or unchecked size for a REF_UNCHECKED node) of the block and of c by the node's length, and either adds the length to the dirty size (converting the block's wasted size to dirty too, unless the block is on bad_used_list, and only if the block is not nextblock and is already dirty or becomes sufficiently dirty) or adds it to the wasted size; it marks the ref REF_OBSOLETE in memory. If JFFS2_SB_FLAG_SCANNING is set it unlocks and returns (693) without refiling the block or rewriting the node on flash (erase_free_sem was not taken). Otherwise it refiles the eraseblock: not moved if it is nextblock; if no used or unchecked bytes remain, it clears c->gcblock or removes it from its list and puts it on erasable_pending_wbuf_list (wbuf dirty), else usually on erase_pending_list (incrementing nr_erasing_blocks and triggering GC) or, when (jiffies & 127) is zero, on erasable_list; not moved if it is the gcblock; moved to dirty_list when newly dirty or to very_dirty_list when newly very dirty. It unlocks erase_completion_lock and returns (755) if marking obsolete on flash is not allowed (not jffs2_can_mark_obsolete, read-only, or BUILDING). Otherwise it reads the node header from flash and, unless the read fails or is short, the stored totlen differs from the ref's length (PAD compared), or the node is already not ACCURATE, it clears JFFS2_NODE_ACCURATE in the header and writes the header back; a write error or short write is only logged and the function goes to out_erase_sem (a partial write may have changed the flash). After a successful write, if ref->next_in_ino is set, under erase_completion_lock it unlinks ref from its inode cache's node list, and for an xattr datum or xattr ref class releases it (CONFIG_JFFS2_FS_XATTR), otherwise deletes the inode cache with jffs2_del_ino_cache when it has no nodes left and pino_nlink is 0. out_erase_sem unlocks c->erase_free_sem.
note: slice cut head (function at 586-842, slice 537-799 ends before the inode-cache unlinking, nodemgmt.c:810-838). reviewers: original right (SCANNING early return at 685-693 before refiling/flash rewrite); round 2 right (a partial write can modify flash, 788-798); round 15 half right: erase_free_sem is taken inside the function (620), but its claim that a successful write does not unlink from the inode cache / release xattrs is wrong: nodemgmt.c:810-838 does both (outside the packet slice).

name: dbDiscardAG
prose: Precondition: ip is the in-core inode of the filesystem, agno names a valid allocation group, minlen is a positive minimum run length in blocks (it is the divisor in do_div), and the caller does not hold the ipbmap write lock (jfs_dmap.c:1571-1651, s64 dbDiscardAG(struct inode *ip, int agno, s64 minlen); the packet had no name). Postcondition: returns the number of blocks trimmed. Return points: 0 at line 1600 if the range array allocation (kmalloc_array of at most 32 * 1024 entries, sized from db_agfree[agno] / minlen + 1) fails, after jfs_error('no memory for trim array') and IWRITE_UNLOCK; otherwise 'return trimmed' at 1650. It takes IWRITE_LOCK(ipbmap, RDWRLOCK_DMAP), then while the requested nblocks is at least minlen it tries dbAllocAG for that many blocks: on 0 it records the allocated range and uses the remaining free count of the AG as the next request (stopping when the AG has no free blocks left); on -ENOSPC it halves the request to the next smaller power of two (stopping if that would go below 1); on any other error it logs jfs_error('-EIO') and stops; it also stops when the array is nearly full (count >= range_cnt - 1). It then releases the lock, and for each recorded range (outside the lock) calls jfs_issue_discard unless the filesystem is mounted with JFS_DISCARD, then dbFree to give the blocks back, adding to the trimmed count; finally it frees the array. The blocks are marked allocated while the lock is held and released afterwards, so other writers cannot use them during the discard.
note: packet item had no name ('(unnamed trim function)'); the slice 1580-1830 includes the body of dbDiscardAG (jfs_dmap.c:1571-1651, slice cut head). No reviewer claim beyond the mechanical one.

name: xtUpdate
prose: Precondition: ip is a JFS inode with an xtree, tid is the transaction id used for logging, nxad is a new XAD (offset, length, address) that lies entirely within an existing extent (normally a not-recorded one) of ip; the caller holds the inode's xtree exclusively (jfs_xtree.c:1513-1936, int xtUpdate(tid_t tid, struct inode *ip, xad_t *nxad); the packet name xtRelocate does not exist, this is xtUpdate which records part of an existing extent). Postcondition: returns 0 on success, or a negative errno. It searches for nxad's offset with xtSearch(..., XT_INSERT) (error returned at 1538), reads the found leaf page, returns -EIO with jfs_error if no entry was found (cmp != 0, 1546) or if nxad is not completely contained within the found XAD (1570), after unpinning the page. It marks the page dirty and, unless COMMIT_Nolink is set, takes an xtree tlock. Then, depending on how nxad sits in the old XAD: if it starts after the XAD start it goes to coalesce/split on the right; if it starts at the XAD start it first tries to merge with the left neighbour when that XAD is recorded, contiguous in offset and address and the merged length is below MAXXLEN (extending the left XAD, marking it XAD_EXTENDED unless XAD_NEW, and either shrinking the old XAD or removing it); otherwise it replaces the old XAD (equal lengths, flag cleared of NOTRECORDED) or splits it into (nXAD, rXAD) at updateLeft. coalesceRight merges nxad with the right neighbour when contiguous and the merged length is below MAXXLEN (truncating or removing the old XAD), else, if the old XAD starts before nxad, splits into (lXAD, nXAD) at updateRight (shortens the old XAD to the not-recorded left part and inserts nXAD, possibly splitting the page with xtSplitUp, and possibly a further three-way split into (lXAD, nXAD, rXAD) by inserting the remainder). jfs_error plus -EIO is also returned for 'xoff >= nxoff' (1699), failed xtSearch repeats (1831), cmp != 0 (1839) and an unexpected index (1846). Other return statements propagate the error of xtSplitUp (1726, 1879) or PTR_ERR from xt_getpage (1731, 1747, 1808, 1884, 1901). On the normal exit (label out) it sets the tlock low-water mark when COMMIT_Nolink is clear, unpins the leaf page and returns rc (0). Errors are not all atomic: some modifications (for example the truncated old XAD at 1712, or the merged neighbour) may already have been made when a later xtSplitUp or xt_getpage error is returned, so the tree is not guaranteed unchanged on failure.
note: packet item was 'xtRelocate' (dropped as not-in-slice); no such function exists. The slice 1532-1790 is the middle of xtUpdate (jfs_xtree.c:1513-1936; slice cut head and tail), so FIXED under the real name per rule 6. The older prose claimed 'relocated' extent and 'tree left unchanged on failure'; both are wrong (the old XAD is truncated at 1712 before xtSplitUp can fail at 1726).

name: xtTruncate
prose: Precondition: ip is a JFS inode whose xtree the caller has exclusively (inode locked); tid is a transaction id (it must be valid whenever flag is COMMIT_PWMAP because the tlock list is used; tid 0 is allowed only for the working-map case), newsize is the new file size in bytes, flag is COMMIT_PWMAP or COMMIT_WMAP once masked with COMMIT_MAP (COMMIT_PMAP is rejected by an assert) (jfs_xtree.c:2203-2732, s64 xtTruncate(tid_t tid, struct inode *ip, s64 newsize, int flag)). Postcondition: returns a size (the value 'newsize', possibly reduced... see below) or a negative errno: PTR_ERR from xt_getpage at lines 2287 and 2525, or -EIO at 2694 if the btstack overflows ('stack overrun'); the normal return is 'return newsize' at 2731. If tid is non-zero tblk->xflag gets the flag. teof is newsize rounded up to blocks. It walks the tree from the root, always visiting the rightmost entries first (processing entries backward, descending through internal pages with BT_PUSH/BT_POP); it clears a non-zero header.next of each visited page. For the leaf level: if the leaf's last extent ends at or before teof the leaf is left alone; with COMMIT_PWMAP and more than MAX_TRUNCATE_LEAVES leaves already locked, it stops processing this leaf and sets newsize = end of the last extent of this leaf, in bytes (which can be larger than the requested newsize, because it is the end of an extent that lies beyond teof), then goes to the parent; otherwise it scans entries backward: entries beyond teof are counted as freed; an entry starting exactly at teof is deleted; an entry spanning teof is shortened (with COMMIT_PWMAP the freed tail is recorded in the tlock, with COMMIT_WMAP it is freed immediately with txFreeMap); the leaf's nextindex is lowered and the page released, then it goes to the parent. If the whole leaf is emptied it is freed (COMMIT_PWMAP: tlock type tlckFREE; COMMIT_WMAP: its extents freed with txFreeMap and the metapage discarded), or, for the root, turned into an empty leaf. Parent pages are processed on the way up: a parent whose child was not emptied has the entries after the current index removed (tlock truncate or txFreeMap); a parent whose child was emptied counts the child's length as freed, has its tlock moved to the end of the tid's tlock list (COMMIT_PWMAP), and is itself freed if it has no remaining entries (the root is converted into an empty leaf and may have its maxentry shrunk to XTROOTINITSLOT with INLINEEA set), otherwise the walk continues with the preceding entry. At out: ip->i_size is set to newsize (or 1 for a directory truncated to 0), dquot_free_block(ip, nfreed) is called, txFreelock(ip) is called when flag is COMMIT_WMAP, and newsize is returned. Errors in xt_getpage at 2525 can occur after COMMIT_WMAP has already freed blocks in the working map with txFreeMap and after pages were modified, so a failed call may have partially truncated the file.
note: slice cut head and tail (function at 2203-2732; the slice 2561-2811 also contains the head of xtTruncate_pmap, which is a different function). reviewer round 15 right: an xt_getpage error at 2525 can come after txFreeMap has modified the working map (2423, 2451, 2481, 2556). The earlier prose also called the early-limit result 'smaller than newsize'; the code sets newsize to the end of the current extent (2334), which can exceed the requested size.

name: xtTruncate_pmap
prose: Precondition: ip is a JFS inode with the xtree held exclusively by the caller; tid is a valid transaction id (tid_to_tblock(tid) is dereferenced); committed_size is 0 or the size in bytes of the committed (persistent-map) file region (jfs_xtree.c:2758-2914, s64 xtTruncate_pmap(tid_t tid, struct inode *ip, s64 committed_size); the packet name xtTruncate belongs to the earlier function at 2203). Postcondition: returns 0 on completion, a positive byte size when it stops early, or a negative errno. It sets COMMIT_PMAP in the transaction's xflag. If committed_size is non-zero it searches the tree for the extent containing the last committed block (xtSearch error returned at 2787; -EIO with jfs_error 'did not find extent' at 2794 if there is no such extent, after XT_PUTPAGE). If committed_size is 0 it starts from the root (xt_getpage error: PTR_ERR at 2810) and descends along the rightmost entries (getChild, with a stack of parents; -EIO with jfs_error 'stack overrun' at 2894 when the stack is full) until a leaf is reached. At the leaf: if the number of leaves locked would exceed MAX_TRUNCATE_LEAVES it returns the end of the extent at the current index, (xoff + xlen) << l2bsize, at 2832, after unpinning the page (so the returned value is the end of the current extent, a value that can be beyond the committed size); otherwise it locks the leaf with a tlckXTREE|tlckFREE tlock (hwm.offset = index) and unpins it. It then goes up (getParent): when the stack is empty it returns 0 (2913); otherwise it reloads the parent page (xt_getpage error: PTR_ERR at 2855); if the parent index is XTENTRYSTART the parent is tlocked with tlckFREE (hwm.offset = last entry), and the walk ends (return 0) if it was the root or continues up; otherwise it moves to the preceding entry and descends again. It does not change the xtree pages' contents or the working map itself (freeing is done at commit by the tlocks).
note: packet record carried the name xtTruncate (2812-2930 is the tail of xtTruncate_pmap, jfs_xtree.c:2758-2914, plus the following function; slice cut head). reviewer round 15 right: the early return at 2832 is the end of the current extent ((xoff + xlen) << l2bsize), which can exceed the committed size, not be smaller. The earlier prose described xtTruncate (a different function) and is replaced.

name: jfs_rename
prose: Precondition: the VFS holds i_rwsem on old_dir and new_dir; old_dentry is positive (old_ip = d_inode), new_dentry may be negative (new_ip NULL); flags may contain only RENAME_NOREPLACE (jfs/namei.c:1068-1349, static int). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno through three return statements: -EINVAL at 1090 if flags has any bit other than RENAME_NOREPLACE (nothing done); -EIO at 1192, taken inside the replace-a-directory branch when the replaced directory's nlink is still non-zero after two drop_nlink calls (it unlocks the commit mutexes and the new_ip write lock if applicable, reports jfs_error, but does NOT call txEnd(tid) or free the UCS names on that path); and 'return rc' at 1348 after the common exit labels. Order of work: dquot_initialize on both directories (error: out1); get_UCSname for both names (errors: out1 / out2); dtSearch of the old name in old_dir must find old_ip->i_ino (else -ENOENT, out3); dtSearch of the new name in new_dir: found with a different inode or no new_ip gives -ESTALE, not found with a new_ip given gives -ESTALE, other dtSearch errors are returned via out3; if old_ip is a directory and new_ip exists it must be empty (dtEmpty, else -ENOTEMPTY); if old_ip is not a directory and new_ip exists, new_ip is write-locked and dquot_initialize'd (error: out_unlock). Then txBegin and the commit mutexes of new_dir, old_ip, old_dir (if different) and new_ip are taken. With an existing target it re-points the directory entry with dtModify (error: out_tx), drops its link count (for a directory twice and, as above, -EIO if still linked; otherwise marks the transaction COMMIT_DELETE; for a file reaching nlink 0 it calls commitZeroLink, aborting the transaction and going to out_tx on a negative result, then COMMIT_DELETE), else updates its ctime. Without an existing target it dtSearch(JFS_CREATE) and dtInsert the new entry (errors: out_tx) and increments new_dir's nlink for a directory moved between directories. It then removes the old entry with dtDelete (error: txAbort and out_tx), adjusts directory link counts and the moved directory's '..' inode and its tlock, updates ctime and mtime, builds the inode list and calls txCommit (COMMIT_SYNC when a file's data still has to be truncated). out_tx: txEnd, unlocks the mutexes, then while new_size is non-zero and rc is 0 it repeatedly truncates the unlinked target with xtTruncate_pmap in new transactions; sets COMMIT_Nolink on new_ip if its nlink is 0; truncates old_dir's directory index table if COMMIT_Stale is set. out_unlock releases the write lock on a non-directory new_ip; out3 and out2 free the two UCS names; out1 logs and returns rc. Failures after txBegin may leave the transaction aborted or partly applied depending on where they occur.
note: slice cut head (function at 1068-1349, slice 1306-1556 covers only its last 44 lines and the next function). reviewer original (precondition describes internal state) partly right: the prose has been rewritten to describe entry state. reviewer round 15 wrong: namei.c:1190-1192 returns -EIO directly without going through out_tx/out3/out2 (no txEnd, no free_UCSname); the other error paths do go through out_tx/out3/out2.

name: jfs_parse_param
prose: Precondition: fc is a filesystem context whose fs_private points to an initialised struct jfs_context; param is one mount parameter (jfs/super.c:250-359, static int). Postcondition: returns 0 if the parameter was accepted and applied, or a negative errno; it only edits the context (flags, uid/gid/umask, nls map, resize request, trim size), not the mounted filesystem. It first calls fs_parse (a negative result is returned at line 260). Then by option: integrity sets JFS_NOINTEGRITY when negated and clears it otherwise; the ignore option does nothing; iocharset unloads a previously loaded nls map (unless it is NULL or the sentinel (void *)-1) and sets ctx->nls_map to NULL for 'none' or to load_nls(name), returning -EINVAL (after the old map was already unloaded) when the charset is not found; resize and resize without size return -EINVAL unless the context is for reconfigure, otherwise set ctx->resize (and newLVSize from the value for the first form); errors replaces the JFS_ERR_MASK bits with the parsed value; with CONFIG_QUOTA quota and usrquota set JFS_USRQUOTA and grpquota sets JFS_GRPQUOTA, while without CONFIG_QUOTA these options only log 'quota operations not supported' and the function still returns 0 with no context change; uid and gid store the parsed ids; umask returns -EINVAL if any bit outside 0777 is set, else stores it; discard sets minblks_trim = 64 and JFS_DISCARD; nodiscard clears JFS_DISCARD; discard_minblk stores minblks_trim and sets JFS_DISCARD; any other option returns -EINVAL (355). Otherwise returns 0 (358).
note: slice cut head and tail (function at 250-359). reviewer round 15 right: without CONFIG_QUOTA the quota options only log an error and return 0 (super.c:313-318).

name: __traverse_mounts
prose: Precondition: the caller holds references on path->dentry and path->mnt, flags is the snapshot of path->dentry->d_flags that includes DCACHE_MANAGED_DENTRY, jumped and count are valid pointers, lookup_flags are the LOOKUP_* flags (namei.c:1468-1527, static int). Postcondition: has one return, 'return ret' at 1526, after writing *jumped = need_mntput (true when at least one mount was crossed). ret is 0, -ENOENT, or a negative errno. The loop runs while the dentry is managed: with DCACHE_MANAGE_TRANSIT it returns -EXDEV (loop exit) if LOOKUP_NO_XDEV is set, otherwise calls the filesystem's d_manage(path, false) and stops with its negative result (flags are reloaded either way); if DCACHE_MOUNTED and lookup_mnt(path) finds a mount in this namespace, it drops the old dentry (and the old mount reference only if it was one this function took earlier) and switches path to the mounted root with new references, sets need_mntput, and stops with -EXDEV if LOOKUP_NO_XDEV is set, else continues; if no automount is pending (no DCACHE_NEED_AUTOMOUNT) the loop ends; otherwise follow_automount(path, count, lookup_flags) is called and a negative result ends the loop with that error (the possible errors include -ELOOP and whatever the automount fails with). After the loop: a result of -EISDIR, from either d_manage or follow_automount, is converted to 0; then, if a mount was crossed and path->mnt is still the mount that was crossed into... precisely, if need_mntput is set and path->mnt equals the original mnt (a possible race with 'mount --move'), the extra mount reference is dropped with mntput; finally, if ret is 0 and the final dentry's flags say it is negative, ret = -ENOENT. On success path holds references to the final dentry and mount (the references on the original ones having been released when crossing).
note: slice cut head (function at 1468-1527, slice 1277-1528). reviewers: original right (the error set includes -EXDEV, -ELOOP from follow_automount and d_manage errors, 1480/1501/1485/1514); round 2 right in part (the old mount reference is released in the loop at 1493-1494, the code at 1521-1522 drops the new one only when it equals the original mnt after racing mount --move); round 15 right: -EISDIR from d_manage is also mapped to 0 (1518-1519).

name: __follow_mount_rcu
prose: Precondition: the caller is in RCU-walk mode with nd->m_seq holding a snapshot of mount_lock's sequence and path->mnt and path->dentry valid under RCU (namei.c:1581-1623, static bool). Postcondition: returns true when the walk can continue with the (possibly updated) path, false when the caller must drop out of RCU mode (a retry or a refwalk). Return points: true at 1587 when the dentry is not managed (nothing changed); false at 1590 if LOOKUP_NO_XDEV is set (any managed dentry); in the loop, when DCACHE_MANAGE_TRANSIT is set it calls d_manage(path, true): a non-zero result returns true if it is -EISDIR (meaning the transit is allowed but the dentry should be used as is) and false otherwise (1600); if DCACHE_MOUNTED and __lookup_mnt finds a mount, path is switched to the mount's root, ND_JUMPED is set in nd->state, nd->next_seq is set to read_seqcount_begin of the new dentry's d_seq, and if mount_lock has changed since nd->m_seq it returns false (1615), else it loops; if DCACHE_MOUNTED is set but no mount is found it returns false if mount_lock changed (1619); finally it returns true unless the final dentry needs an automount (1621: !(flags & DCACHE_NEED_AUTOMOUNT)). nd->next_seq and ND_JUMPED are changed only when a mount is crossed (1609-1610), not on every true return; the function takes no references.
note: slice cut head (function at 1581-1623). reviewers: original right (false on LOOKUP_NO_XDEV, 1589-1590); round 2 right (true when a managed dentry has no mount and no NEED_AUTOMOUNT, 1621); round 15 right (next_seq set only when crossing a mount, 1610).

name: link_path_walk
prose: Precondition: name is a NUL-terminated pathname or an ERR_PTR value (the result of getname-style setup), nd is a nameidata initialised by path_init, with nd->path and nd->inode set (namei.c:2470-2566, static int). Postcondition: returns 0 when the walk has reached the parent of the last component (nd->last, nd->last_type set, nd->path/nd->inode being the parent directory), or a negative errno; it does not drop the nameidata's path references on any return (the caller's terminate_walk does, and in RCU mode it does not take references either). Return points: PTR_ERR(name) at 2478 if name is an error pointer; 0 at 2486 for an empty path after leading slashes (nd->dir_mode set to 0); the error of may_lookup (lookup permission, which may be -ECHILD in RCU mode) at 2498; a negative d_hash result at 2521 for filesystems with DCACHE_OP_HASH; 0 at 2541 after the last component of the top-level path (depth 0), where it records dir_vfsuid and dir_mode of the parent, clears LOOKUP_PARENT; PTR_ERR(link) at 2552 when walk_component returns an error pointer; -ECHILD at 2561 if the current dentry cannot be looked up in RCU mode and try_to_unlazy fails; -ENOTDIR at 2563 otherwise when the current dentry is not a directory. Loop: for each component it checks may_lookup, records nd->last.name, hashes the name (hash_name sets last_type LAST_DOTDOT with ND_JUMPED, LAST_DOT or LAST_NORM with ND_JUMPED cleared and the optional d_hash call), skips slashes; at the last component of the path (or of a nested symlink body) it either finishes (depth 0) or pops the saved name and walks the component with walk_component(nd, 0); for other components it calls walk_component(nd, WALK_MORE). If walk_component returns a symlink body it pushes the remaining name on nd->stack, continues with the link text as the name, and the depth is increased.
note: slice cut head (function at 2470-2566, slice 2315-2567). reviewers: original right (the contract omitted error paths); round 15 right: link_path_walk never releases references itself (returns at 2478-2563 just return err); cleanup is by the caller.

name: atomic_open
prose: Precondition: nd is an initialised nameidata whose path.dentry is the parent directory (its inode supports ->atomic_open), dentry is the (in-lookup) child dentry holding a reference the function consumes, file is the struct file being opened, open_flag the open flags and mode the creation mode (namei.c:3672-3710, static struct dentry *). The caller need not initialise file->f_path: the function sets file->__f_path.dentry to the sentinel DENTRY_NOT_SET ((void *)-1) and file->__f_path.mnt to nd->path.mnt before the call. Postcondition: returns a dentry pointer or an ERR_PTR; single return at 3709. It adds O_DIRECTORY if LOOKUP_DIRECTORY is set, calls dir->i_op->atomic_open with the open flags converted by open_to_namei_flags, and then d_lookup_done(dentry). If the call returned 0: when FMODE_OPENED is set in file->f_mode (the file was opened), the returned dentry is dentry, or file->f_path.dentry (with dput of the old and dget of the new) if they differ, with no check that the result is positive (the d_is_negative test is not applied on this branch); when the file was not opened, if file->f_path.dentry is still DENTRY_NOT_SET it WARNs and sets error = -EIO; otherwise, if the filesystem returned a different dentry in file->f_path.dentry (non-NULL), it replaces dentry with it (dput of the old reference, ownership of the new one passes), and if the resulting dentry is negative the error is -ENOENT.
